opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll; full-time employees may have up to write, and admin is not permitted since Engineer does not own Payroll. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E045 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. With basic training, maximum access is read. Requested write, so grant read.
reason: The Security agent's record shows E045 (Douglas Salinas) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. With basic training, the maximum allowed access to Payroll is read. The requested write exceeds the max, so grant the maximum of read. (Note: HR's record lists the employee as full-time, but the security record governs access entitlement, and read is at or below the maximum under either interpretation.)
